intro: Saturday brings clearer version boundaries for local AI, a robotics walkthrough and a December migration deadline. South Coast rivers are receding, factory volumes have weakened, and December planning offers global holiday music, creative technology and a festive dinner.

stories.title: llama.cpp gives developers clearer version boundaries
stories.summary: The llama.cpp and ggml libraries released version 1.0.0 Friday, committing to major-version changes when public interfaces become incompatible. Developers embedding local inference gain clearer signals for breaking updates as they maintain applications across hardware and model backends.

stories.title: NVIDIA assembles a simulated pick-and-place task
stories.summary: NVIDIA published an Isaac Sim walkthrough combining a robot arm, gripper and beverage can from its SimReady asset library. The example separates validated physical properties from task controls, showing builders how to assemble a scene and test its behaviour.

stories.title: Six Copilot models face December retirement
stories.summary: GitHub will retire six listed Copilot models on December 14, with suggested alternatives for five. Review workflows and organization policies before switching; annual individual subscribers retain Claude Haiku 4.5 under an exception, while Kimi K3’s replacement remains unannounced.

stories.title: Copilot app adds general Enterprise Server support
stories.summary: GitHub Enterprise Server support is generally available in Copilot app version 1.2.0 and later, covering remote repositories, issues and pull requests. Sign in with a cloud account first, then add the server account through settings; cloud sessions remain unavailable.

stories.title: South Coast flood watch steps down
stories.summary: The River Forecast Centre downgraded Howe Sound, Sea-to-Sky and the North Shore Mountains to a high streamflow advisory Friday. Rivers were receding, but adjacent floodwaters could linger; stay clear of swift riverbanks and never drive across flooded crossings.

stories.title: Three deaths confirmed after boating incident
stories.summary: Squamish RCMP confirmed Friday that three people died following Thursday’s boating incident and that everyone was accounted for. Elevated water and debris complicated recovery efforts; police asked the public to stay off local waterways while dangerous conditions continued.

stories.title: Flat factory sales conceal falling volumes
stories.summary: Canadian manufacturing sales held at $80.2 billion in September but fell 1.5% after adjusting for prices, Statistics Canada reported Friday. Petroleum gains offset weaker metals and wood products; excluding petroleum and coal products, nominal sales also declined 1.5%.

events.title: Sultans of String bring Christmas Caravan to Kitsilano
events.description: The seasonal concert combines original music with global arrangements of holiday favourites, joined by Rebecca Campbell and Saskia Tomkins. Advance hall admission is $32, rising to $37 at the door; doors open at seven for the all-ages performance.

meetups.title: AI Film Club makes room for unfinished work
meetups.description: Kevin Friel hosts screenings, tool demonstrations and workflow discussions for filmmakers and creative technologists. Bring a clip, a problem or a laptop to demonstrate your process; community tickets are $20, with free admission for verified BC + AI members.

dining.title: Notch8 lists its Christmas Eve feast
dining.description: The multi-course menu includes lobster with vanilla bisque and egg-yolk raviolo with winter truffle. Adults pay $315 including taxes, fees and 18% gratuity; reservations require non-refundable prepayment, and each seating lasts two and a half hours.
